children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures eased on Wednesday as traders waited to see results from U.S. harvests, following an improvement in the crop's condition rating this week.
Traders were uncertain about the crop's yields due to hot weather last month.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture lowered its production and yield estimates in a monthly report on Friday. However, the agency raised the crop's good-excellent rating by 1 percentage point in a weekly report on Monday.
"The corn market is just on hold here," said Don Roose, president of brokerage U.S. Commodities. "It's up to the combine here."

The USDA said on Monday that farmers had harvested 8% of the nation's corn crop and 6% of the soybean crop so far.
Rains in parts of the upper Midwest have slowed harvesting, said Brian Hoops, president of Midwest Market Solutions.
"It appears to be funds are looking to unwind some of their net long positions in the grains as we begin harvest activities," he said.
"Forecasts suggest activity will begin again next week and funds are interested in shedding market length without pressuring values too much."
Weaker oil prices and lingering hopes of diplomatic progress to resolve war disruptions to Black Sea grain trade also hung over the grain markets.

Traders were waiting to see whether China ramps up purchases of U.S. soybeans in conjunction with an expected meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Washington next week.
"Limited export news this week for soybeans seems to be capping rallies as buying interest is slowing at these higher price levels," Hoops said.
On Thursday, the USDA is slated to issue weekly U.S. grain and soybean export sales data.
